summary: Matt Patches argues that Danny Elfman's stint voicing and singing as Jack Skellington in The Nightmare Before Christmas led to his reinvention as a shirtless rock-star performer, culminating in his 2022 Coachella set. The piece traces his Oingo Boingo roots, his film and concert work, the Nightmare concerts at the Hollywood Bowl, and the Big Mess album. It also notes a 2018 sexual misconduct lawsuit, settled out of court, which Elfman denies.
one_line: Polygon argues that playing Jack Skellington in The Nightmare Before Christmas set Danny Elfman on the path to his 2022 Coachella rock-star turn.
key_facts: Danny Elfman played Coachella in 2022, performing shirtless, and Vulture wrote that "Nobody else even came close to bringing that level of chaotic pageantry."
Before composing for Tim Burton, Elfman was in the new wave band Oingo Boingo, founded by his brother Richard; its biggest hit was the 1985 single "Weird Science."
Oingo Boingo toured and recorded through the early '90s, and members of the band still tour today.
Elfman recorded demos for Jack Skellington's songs in The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993), then sang the final versions; Chris Sarandon was hired to match his baritone in the spoken dialogue.
Elfman received four Oscar nominations, for Good Will Hunting, Men in Black, Big Fish, and Milk.

In 2005 Elfman premiered Serenada Schizophrana, his first work composed specifically for concert orchestra; in 2008 he wrote music for the American Ballet Theatre's Rabbit and Rogue; in 2011 he composed for Cirque Du Soleil's $100 million Iris show.
In 2013 Elfman performed his Tim Burton scores with a full orchestra at the Royal Albert Hall, singing select Nightmare Before Christmas numbers in full (a correction notes it was 2013, not 2014).
Disney invited Elfman, Catherine O'Hara (Sally) and Ken Page (Oogie Boogie) to a Nightmare Before Christmas concert at the Hollywood Bowl, which has been repeated every October.
After seeing Childish Gambino and Janelle Monáe at Coachella 2019, the then-66-year-old Elfman began building a set mixing film music, Oingo Boingo hits and experimental songs.
Coachella 2020 was canceled due to COVID-19; Elfman released the studio album Big Mess and played Coachella in 2022.
At Coachella Elfman said it was "my first time onstage as 'myself' in 27 years."
Earlier in 2023 a Rolling Stone report uncovered a 2018 sexual misconduct lawsuit against Elfman, settled out of court; he called the accusations "vicious and wholly false."
Elfman later scored White Noise for Noah Baumbach and performed his Coachella act at the North Island Credit Union Amphitheatre in California.
